title: Spatial-Order Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Exchange-Correlation Potential
abstract: Exact time-dependent density-functional theory separates the exchange-correlation potential into interaction and kinetic-correlation components, but the structural relation between them remains unknown. We establish a representability constraint based on the off-diagonal expansion of the one-electron reduced density matrix relative to a time-dependent Hartree-Fock (TDHF) reference. A non-zero linear term generates a non-HF current density while the kinetic-correlation component remains HF representable; higher-order off-diagonal structure activates the kinetic component. In a one-dimensional two-electron correlation quench, retaining the exact interaction component while setting the kinetic component to zero suppresses the density broadening of the exact evolution. These results establish a hierarchy of density equations of motion and provide an exact constraint for non-adiabatic functional construction.
summary: This paper tackles the unknown structural link between interaction and kinetic components within TDDFT's exchange-correlation potential. Using 1RDM expansions and numerical simulations on a 1D model, it derives mathematical constraints proving that accurate description of non-adiabatic electron motion requires incorporating these kinetic correlation terms. This provides an exact guiding principle for developing next-generation quantum simulation functionals.
main_problem: The core problem is establishing a rigorous structural relationship between the kinetic-correlation ($v_{T}^{c}$) and interaction components of the time-dependent exchange-correlation potential ($v_{xc}$) within TDDFT.
main_result: The analysis establishes mathematical constraints derived from the off-diagonal expansion of the one-body reduced density matrix, proving that non-trivial kinetic correlation terms are necessary for accurate description during non-adiabatic dynamics.
method: The authors employ a combination of theoretical derivation using 1RDM expansions and numerical simulation on a 1D two-electron model to test different approximations for $v_{xc}$.
model_or_system: The study uses general N-electron systems, with specific quantitative tests performed on a one-dimensional two-electron spin-singlet model analogous to a 1D helium system.
key_observables: Electron density evolution ($\Theta(x, t)$), the effective force field ($F_{	ext{eff}}$), and the difference between exact and Hartree-Fock reduced density matrices ($\Delta\hat{\gamma}(t)$).
important_parameters: Time scales (e.g., $t=5.0$ a.u.), spatial dimensions (1D), and the order of expansion in the 1RDM off-diagonal distance.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on expanding the 1RDM relative to the TDHF reference, and while it addresses non-adiabatic dynamics, some derivations utilize structural constraints derived from low-order Taylor expansions.
figures_summary: Figures compare contours of the cumulative density function $\Theta(x, t)$ showing differences between exact time evolution (red solid) and truncated propagation results.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the components of $v_{xc}$ via 1RDM structure; it then establishes a mathematical constraint linking these components using low-order expansions; finally, numerical simulations on a 1D model demonstrate the physical consequences of neglecting kinetic correlation terms.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental theoretical constraints for constructing accurate time-dependent functionals beyond standard approximations, which is crucial for simulating complex quantum dynamics in condensed matter systems.
